title: Bicolandia Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Bicolandia Marathon 2026 Review: Midnight Start, Small Field
meta_description: Bicolandia Marathon 2026 review: a 12.20am start in Sorsogon City, 25°C and near-saturated air, 24 marathon finishers and how fast the field ran.
dek: What the 2026 Bicolandia Marathon in Sorsogon City was like to run: the night-time starts, the race-morning weather and how fast a very small field finished.
verdict: Enter if you want a quiet, low-key marathon at the southern tip of Luzon and are happy to run through the night. The 2026 marathon started at 12.20am, which kept the whole race in air of about 25°C, though the humidity sat near 100% with almost no wind. The field is tiny: 24 marathoners finished, half of them after 5 hours 22 minutes, so expect long stretches alone. The organiser published little beyond the results, so ask for the route and cut-offs before booking travel.

sections.heading: The Start: A Marathon Run Through the Night
paragraphs: The 2026 race started and finished at Our Lady of Peñafrancia Seminary in Sorsogon City, and the results put the marathon gun at 12.20am on Sunday 27 September. The half marathon followed at 3.30am, the 10 km at 4.30am and the 5 km at 5.30am [1].

Even the last marathoner home finished at 6.55am, so the marathon is run almost entirely in the dark. No route map or course description was published with the results [1], so a light, something reflective and a look at the route before race day are sensible.

sections.heading: The Weather: Warm, Saturated and Still
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's modelled hourly weather for Sorsogon City gives about 25°C at the midnight start, with a dew point of 25°C, 97% to 99% humidity and wind under 5 km/h. It barely moved through the night: 24.7°C and 98% humidity from 3am to 6am, under thick cloud and with no rain [2].

The change came after sunrise: 26.8°C and 91% humidity at 7am, then 29.6°C at 8am [2]. Every marathoner finished before 7am, so the night start did its job. Half marathoners and 10 km runners at the back met the warming air: the last half-marathon finisher came in at 7.24am. With the air this wet, sweat barely evaporates, so pace for the humidity rather than the temperature.

sections.heading: Cut-offs and Finishing Times
paragraphs: No cut-off times were published with the results. The slowest recorded finishes were 6:34:51 in the marathon, 3:54:15 in the half marathon and 2:27:30 in the 10 km [1]. Results are given as gun times; with such small fields, gun and chip time differ little.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Only 24 runners finished the marathon. Two broke four hours, both in about 3:13, and the next runner was another 51 minutes back; tenth place was 4:57:48. Ten of the 24 finished inside five hours, the median was 5:22:12 and the 90th percentile 6:22:01. Four of the finishers were women, the fastest in 4:10:37 [1].

The half marathon had 82 finishers. Three men finished within 1:16:06, but tenth place was already 1:59:14; the median was 2:42:37 and the 90th percentile 3:18:35. Eleven runners (13%) broke two hours and 32 (39%) broke 2:30. Women made up 35% of the field [1].

The 10 km had the biggest field, 157 finishers, and more than half of them (54%) were women. Its median was 1:39:39, and only eight runners finished inside an hour, so many 10 km entrants walked much of it [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Bicolandia Marathon?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want an unhurried provincial marathon where a night start keeps the heat away and a sub-four-hour time puts you near the front. In 2026, any marathoner under five hours finished in the top half, and a 2:30 half marathon was faster than six runners in ten.

Think twice if you need company on the road, a published route, or the support of a big-city race: with 24 marathon finishers, gaps of several minutes between runners are normal. Ask the organiser for the route, aid-station plan and cut-offs before entering, since none were published with the 2026 results.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the official results and modelled historical weather.

faqs.question: What time does the Bicolandia Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2026 the marathon started at 12.20am on Sunday 27 September, the half marathon at 3.30am, the 10 km at 4.30am and the 5 km at 5.30am, all from Our Lady of Peñafrancia Seminary in Sorsogon City. These times come from the official results, so check the organiser's notice for the next edition.

faqs.question: How hot is the Bicolandia Marathon?
faqs.answer: Warm and very humid rather than hot, because the marathon runs at night. Modelled weather for Sorsogon City in 2026 gave about 25°C, a 25°C dew point and 97% to 99% humidity from midnight to 6am, with almost no wind. It reached 27°C at 7am and 30°C by 8am, after every marathoner had finished.

faqs.question: How fast is the field at the Bicolandia Marathon?
faqs.answer: Small and spread out. In 2026, 24 runners finished the marathon: two in about 3:13, tenth place in 4:57:48 and the median in 5:22:12. The half marathon had 82 finishers with a median of 2:42:37, and 39% of them finished under 2:30. A sub-five-hour marathon put you in the top half.
